summary: Adams County, WI tower that FFLA lists as gone. No build, staffing or removal record found; story uses 2015 statewide DNR background only.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists it as gone. No source gives a removal date or method.

evidence.supports: Hickey Bluff listed under Adams County as a tower, status Gone, at 43.82138 -89.70978
Hickey Bluff on the FFLA alphabetical list: Adams County, Tower, Gone
State's fire towers built in the 1930s and 1940s
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930's and 1940's, the towers at the time were the front line to protect Wisconsin's forests.

evidence.supports: 119 towers staffed around Wisconsin in their heyday
evidence.quote: In their heyday, the there were 119 towers staffed around Wisconsin.

evidence.supports: DNR announced the fire towers were being eliminated, December 2015
evidence.quote: The DNR announced late last week the fire towers used to spot out of control fires were being eliminated.

evidence.supports: Cost of replacing towers and modern technology were factors in the decision
evidence.quote: the cost of replacing the towers and modern technology were factors in their demise

evidence.supports: DNR staffed 60 fire lookout towers the year before the announcement
evidence.quote: Last year, the DNR staffed 60 fire lookout towers

evidence.supports: DNR planned to discontinue using the fire towers across the state
evidence.quote: to discontinue using the fire lookout towers it has scattered throughout the state

evidence.supports: Many towers stand in easements on private property
evidence.quote: Many of the towers stand in easements that have been granted on private property.

evidence.supports: Property owners might choose to take over towers standing in easements
evidence.quote: In those cases, Marty said, the property owners might simply choose to take over the towers.

sources.title: State Fire Towers To Leave The Landscape

notes_for_editor: Only the two FFLA listings name this tower (gone, Adams County, coordinates). WXPR and Daily Reporter are statewide DNR background; neither names Hickey Bluff, so the story does not connect it to the 2015 decision. Two web searches and the local caches turned up no build, staffing or removal record.
